apps.name: Visual Studio Code
apps.what: Usage events, error telemetry and crash reports sent to Microsoft. Extensions send their own telemetry, which the same setting gates.

steps: Set "telemetry.telemetryLevel": "off" in settings.json (Preferences > Settings > search for telemetry).
Start the editor with --disable-telemetry for a single run.

apps.name: Cursor
apps.what: VS Code fork. Sends editor telemetry, plus prompt and code data unless Privacy Mode is on.

steps: Turn on Privacy Mode in Cursor Settings > General to stop code and prompts leaving the machine.

apps.name: VSCodium
apps.what: VS Code build with the Microsoft telemetry endpoints removed. Extensions can still report on their own.

steps: Telemetry is off in the build. Keep "telemetry.telemetryLevel": "off" to also mute extensions.

apps.name: JetBrains IDEs (IntelliJ, PyCharm, WebStorm, ...)
apps.what: The Data Sharing option sends feature usage statistics to JetBrains.

steps: Settings > Appearance & Behavior > System Settings > Data Sharing: clear all boxes.
For a fleet, ship an idea.properties with the Data Sharing consent already declined.

apps.name: Android Studio / Android SDK tools
apps.what: Sends usage statistics and crash reports to Google. The setting also covers the SDK command line tools.

steps: Settings > Appearance & Behavior > System Settings > Data Sharing: clear the box.

apps.name: Zed
apps.what: Sends metrics (feature usage) and diagnostics (crash reports).

apps.name: Neovim / Vim
apps.what: No telemetry in the editor. Plugins and language servers can still call home.

steps: Nothing to turn off. Audit the plugins and language servers you install.

apps.name: Homebrew
apps.what: Sends anonymous install and build events to a Homebrew owned InfluxDB.

steps: Or export HOMEBREW_NO_ANALYTICS=1 in your shell profile.

apps.name: npm
apps.what: No usage telemetry. The registry still sees your install requests, and the update notifier calls out on its own.

steps: To mute the update check: export NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER=1, or npm config set update-notifier false.
Use --no-audit and --no-fund to stop the extra registry calls on install.

apps.name: Yarn (Berry, v2+)
apps.what: Sends anonymous usage counts of the packages you install.

steps: Run in the project: yarn config set --home enableTelemetry 0

apps.name: pnpm
apps.what: No telemetry.

apps.name: .NET SDK / CLI
apps.what: The dotnet command sends command name, timing, OS and hardware data to Microsoft.

steps: Set DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT=1 in the environment of every shell and build agent.

apps.name: PowerShell (7+)
apps.what: Sends the OS name and PowerShell version at start up to Microsoft.

apps.name: Go toolchain
apps.what: Go 1.23+ keeps counter files on disk (mode local). Uploads only happen if you opt in with mode on.

steps: Run: go telemetry off (this also deletes the local counter files).

apps.name: winget
apps.what: Sends usage events to Microsoft.

steps: Run: winget settings, then add "telemetry": { "disable": true }.
Windows wide diagnostic data settings also apply.

apps.name: Composer
apps.what: No telemetry. Packagist sees the package requests it serves.

apps.name: Rust (cargo, rustup)
apps.what: No telemetry in the toolchain.

apps.name: Deno
apps.what: No telemetry by default. Deno only sends OpenTelemetry data if you start it with OTEL_DENO=1.

apps.name: Next.js
apps.what: Records build and dev commands, feature use, and general machine data for Vercel.

apps.name: Gatsby
apps.what: Sends build timings, plugin names and machine data.

apps.name: Nuxt
apps.what: Sends anonymous build and module usage data.

steps: Or set telemetry: false in nuxt.config.ts.

apps.name: Astro
apps.what: Sends anonymous data about the config and integrations you build with.

apps.name: Angular CLI
apps.what: Sends command usage and build data to Google Analytics.

apps.name: Storybook
apps.what: Sends anonymous usage of builders, framework and addons.

apps.name: Turborepo
apps.what: Sends anonymous command and feature usage to Vercel.

apps.name: Strapi
apps.what: Sends anonymous project and usage events.

steps: Add "telemetryDisabled": true under the "strapi" key of package.json.

apps.name: RedwoodJS
apps.what: Sends anonymous CLI command and error data.

steps: Set REDWOOD_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1, or pass --no-telemetry to the CLI.

apps.name: Expo / EAS CLI
apps.what: Sends anonymous CLI usage events.

steps: Set EXPO_NO_TELEMETRY=1 in your shell profile and in CI.

apps.name: Ionic CLI
apps.what: Sends anonymous command usage.

steps: Run: ionic config set -g telemetry false

apps.name: Apache Cordova
apps.what: Sends anonymous command usage to Google Analytics.

apps.name: Flutter / Dart SDK
apps.what: Sends command usage and crash data to Google.

apps.name: Prisma
apps.what: Uses the HashiCorp checkpoint client for version checks, which sends a request with machine data.

steps: Set CHECKPOINT_DISABLE=1 in your shell profile and in CI.

apps.name: Cypress
apps.what: Sends crash reports and exception data during test runs.

steps: Set CYPRESS_COMMERCIAL_RECOMMENDATIONS=0 to mute the product prompts.

apps.name: Playwright
apps.what: No usage telemetry. It does download browser builds from a Microsoft CDN.

apps.name: Vite
apps.what: No telemetry.

apps.name: Terraform
apps.what: The HashiCorp checkpoint service gets a version check with an anonymous machine ID on most commands.

apps.name: Packer
apps.what: Same HashiCorp checkpoint version call as Terraform.

apps.name: Vagrant
apps.what: Checks for updates through the HashiCorp checkpoint service.

apps.name: Google Cloud CLI (gcloud)
apps.what: Sends anonymous command usage to Google.

steps: Run: gcloud config set disable_usage_reporting true

apps.name: Azure CLI
apps.what: Sends command name, parameters used, errors and timing to Microsoft.

apps.name: AWS SAM CLI
apps.what: Sends command usage and error data to AWS.

apps.name: AWS CDK
apps.what: Version reporting adds a CDKMetadata resource to every stack, which tells AWS which constructs you use.

steps: Or pass --no-version-reporting to each cdk command.

apps.name: Serverless Framework
apps.what: Sends anonymous command and service data.

apps.name: Netlify CLI
apps.what: Sends anonymous command usage.

apps.name: Vercel CLI
apps.what: Sends anonymous command usage to Vercel.

apps.name: Firebase CLI
apps.what: Sends anonymous CLI usage to Google Analytics.

steps: Run: firebase logout, then answer No to usage reporting on the next login.
Or set "usage": false in the configstore file.

apps.name: Cloudflare Wrangler
apps.what: Sends anonymous command usage to Cloudflare.

apps.name: Stripe CLI
apps.what: Sends anonymous command usage to Stripe.

apps.name: Salesforce CLI (sf)
apps.what: Sends command usage and error data to Salesforce.

apps.name: Snyk CLI
apps.what: Sends anonymous analytics about CLI runs.

apps.name: Hasura CLI / GraphQL Engine
apps.what: Sends anonymous usage of the CLI, console and server.

apps.name: MongoDB Shell (mongosh)
apps.what: Sends anonymous usage events to MongoDB.

apps.name: Docker Desktop
apps.what: Sends usage statistics and crash reports to Docker.

steps: Docker Desktop > Settings > General: clear "Send usage statistics".
Fleet wide: set analyticsEnabled to false in the settings JSON, or use the admin settings file.

apps.name: Docker CLI (hints and Scout)
apps.what: The CLI prints Docker Scout hints and checks for advice, which contacts Docker.

steps: Set "hints": false in ~/.docker/config.json, or export DOCKER_CLI_HINTS=false.

apps.name: Grafana (self hosted)
apps.what: Reports anonymous usage statistics and checks for updates.

steps: In grafana.ini set [analytics] reporting_enabled = false, check_for_updates = false and check_for_plugin_updates = false.

apps.name: Netdata
apps.what: Sends anonymous usage statistics from the agent.

steps: Create the file /etc/netdata/.opt-out-from-anonymous-statistics and restart netdata.

apps.name: Mozilla Firefox
apps.what: Sends technical and interaction data (Telemetry), plus crash reports and Firefox Suggest data.

steps: Settings > Privacy & Security > Firefox Data Collection and Use: clear every box.
Fleet wide: set DisableTelemetry to true in the policies.json enterprise policy.

apps.name: Google Chrome
apps.what: Usage statistics and crash reports go to Google when the metrics option is on.

steps: Settings > You and Google > Sync and Google services: turn off "Help improve Chrome's features and performance".
Fleet wide: set the MetricsReportingEnabled policy to false.

apps.name: Brave
apps.what: P3A privacy preserving analytics and crash reports. No Google metrics.

steps: Settings > Privacy and security: turn off product analytics (P3A), diagnostic reports and daily usage ping.

apps.name: Microsoft Edge
apps.what: Sends browsing and usage diagnostic data to Microsoft.

steps: Settings > Privacy, search, and services: turn off the optional diagnostic data and personalization options.
Fleet wide: set the MetricsReportingEnabled policy to false.

apps.name: Chromium
apps.what: Most distribution builds ship without the Google metrics keys, but the switch is the same.

steps: Settings > Privacy and security: turn off usage statistics and crash reports.

apps.name: macOS analytics (Apple)
apps.what: Shares Mac analytics, crash data and Siri data with Apple.

steps: System Settings > Privacy & Security > Analytics & Improvements: turn off every option.

apps.name: Ubuntu crash reports (apport / whoopsie)
apps.what: apport collects crash data and whoopsie uploads it to Canonical.

steps: Set enabled=0 in /etc/default/apport and run: sudo systemctl stop apport
Set report_crashes=false in /etc/default/whoopsie, or remove the whoopsie package.

apps.name: Windows diagnostic data
apps.what: Windows sends required and optional diagnostic data to Microsoft.

steps: Settings > Privacy & security > Diagnostics & feedback: turn off optional diagnostic data and tailored experiences.
Pro and Enterprise: set the Group Policy Allow Telemetry (AllowTelemetry) to the lowest level your edition supports.

apps.name: Syncthing
apps.what: Optional anonymous usage reporting to the Syncthing project.

steps: Web UI > Settings: set Anonymous Usage Reporting to No (this writes urAccepted -1).

apps.name: Insomnia
apps.what: Sends usage analytics to Kong.

steps: Preferences > General: clear "Send usage statistics" and "Send error reports".

apps.name: Slack desktop
apps.what: Client usage is logged server side. There is no local opt-out switch.

steps: No local switch. Workspace owners on paid plans control the analytics and retention settings.
Block third party trackers at the network level if this matters to you.

apps.name: Zoom
apps.what: Product usage and quality data go to Zoom.

steps: Zoom web portal > Settings: turn off the product usage and marketing data options your account exposes.
There is no local file to flip.

apps.name: Claude Code
apps.what: Sends usage telemetry and error reports to Anthropic.

steps: Or set CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1 to cover all of them.
These can also live in the "env" block of ~/.claude/settings.json.

apps.name: Gemini CLI
apps.what: Sends usage statistics to Google.

apps.name: GitHub Copilot
apps.what: Code snippets and suggestion events can be kept by GitHub for product improvement.

steps: Turn off editor telemetry (see the vscode entry).
In GitHub settings > Copilot, turn off "Allow GitHub to use my code snippets for product improvements".
Organisation owners set the same policy for all members.
